0.note: The word translated as **chief musician** likely refers to the person in charge of music for worship. Some languages may have a term for a music leader. Alternate translation: [For the music director] or [For the leader of worship music]

1.note: David is speaking of **transgression** as if it were a living thing that could speak a **declaration** to the wicked. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Sin causes a person to act like they are listening to bad advice within themselves]

If your language does not use an abstract nouns for the idea of **declaration** and **transgression**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [What rebelling against God declares]

David is using the adjective **wicked** as a noun to mean a certain kind of person. Your language may use adjectives in the same way. If not, you can translate this adjective with an equivalent phrase. Alternate translation: [to those who are wicked]

The phrase **my heart** is a translation of the majority of Hebrew manuscripts. Other Hebrew manuscripts and ancient translations say, “his heart,” which seems to make better sense. The UST follows that reading. You may want to follow the major translation in your area. Alternate translation: [is in the midst of his heart]

Here the **heart** represents where a person’s thoughts and understanding exist. You may have a comparable expression in your language, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [is in his deepest understanding]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **dread**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [reverence for]

Here, **before his eyes** represents the wicked person’s awareness. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [in his awareness]
The pronoun **his** refers to the wicked person. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [the wicked person’s eyes]

2.note: The word translated as **For** indicates that what follows is a reason for what came before. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that what follows is a reason for what came before. Alternate translation: [Because]

David is describing the way that a wicked person flatters himself and is proud by saying that recognizing his sin **is slippery to him in his eyes**, that is, his pride blinds him to it and he convinces himself that he is not sinful. If this image communicates well in your language, please use it. If not, you could express this in another way. Alternate translation: [he flatters himself too much]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **iniquity**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [to acknowledge that he acts wrongly]
The pronoun **it** refers to the wicked person’s sin. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [so he hates his sin]

3.note: David is using the phrase **words of his mouth** to represent what the wicked person said by using words. If it would be clearer in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [The things he says]

The terms **iniquity** and **deceit** mean similar things. David is using the two terms together for emphasis. If it would be clearer for your readers, you could express the emphasis with a single phrase. Alternate translation: [thoroughly wicked speech]
If your language does not use abstract nouns for the ideas of **iniquity** and **deceit**, you could express the same ideas in other ways. Alternate translation: [are what is wicked and deceptive]

These two phrases **to act wisely** and **to do good** mean basically the same thing. David is using the two terms together for emphasis. If it would be clearer for your readers, you could express the emphasis with a single phrase. Alternate translation: [he has completely ceased to do things that are good]

4.note: If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **iniquity**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [how to act wickedly]

David is speaking of how the wicked person commits to a bad way of living as if it were a **not-good road** that he chose and that he **stations himself on**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [he commits himself to a wicked way of living]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **evil**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [doing wicked things]

5.note: David is speaking as if Yahweh’s covenant faithfulness were so vast that it fills **the heavens**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [your covenant faithfulness is immeasurably great]

If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **covenant faithfulness**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [how faithful you are to your covenant]

David is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [your trustworthiness extends to the clouds]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **trustworthiness**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [how trustworthy you are]

6.note: The point of this comparison is that just as **the mountains of God** are immovable and enduring, so is his **righteousness**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could make this point explicitly. Alternate translation: [Your righteousness is as enduring as the highest mountains]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **righteousness**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [The way you do what is right]

David is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [your judgments are like the great deep]

David is using another comparison to describe Yahweh’s ways. The point of this comparison is that just as **the great deep** or the deepest ocean is vast and mysterious, so are God’s **judgments**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could make this point explicitly. Alternate translation: [your judgments are as immeasurable and unsearchable as the deepest ocean]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **judgments**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [the way you act justly]

7.note: If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **covenant faithfulness**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [is the way you are faithful to your covenant]

David is using **the sons of man** as a common expression of the culture to mean “human beings.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [And people]

David is speaking of God’s protection as if he were a bird that provides a **refuge** or protection under **the shadow of** its **wings**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [can find their protection in you]

8.note: The pronoun **They** refers to “the sons of man” or people mentioned in verse 7. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [People are refreshed]
If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [You refresh them]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **fatness**, you could express the same ideas in other ways. Alternate translation: [from all that you so abundantly provide]

David is speaking as if God’s blessings were a **river** of **delights** that people could **drink** from. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and they experience the abundance of your blessings]

9.note: David is speaking as if God were a **fountain** from which **life** flows. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [is the source of life]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **life**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [the ability to live]

David is speaking as if God’s presence were **light** that enables people to see **light**, representing understanding. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [because you reveal yourself to us, we are able to understand truth]

10.note: If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **covenant faithfulness**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [the way you are faithful to your covenant]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **righteousness**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [and how you do what is right]

David is using the adjective **upright** as a noun to mean a certain kind of person. Your language may use adjectives in the same way. If not, you could translate this with an equivalent expression. Alternate translation: [to those who are upright in heart]

Here the **heart** represents where a person’s motives and intentions exist. You may have a comparable expression in your language, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [to those who have right intentions]

11.note: David is expressing a wish to God. In your translation, use a form that people would recognize as a wish or request in your language. You might express this as a prayer, if that would be more natural in your language. Alternate translation: [Please keep the foot of pride from coming to me, and the hand of the wicked from removing me]

Here, **the foot** represents the power to trample or overcome another person. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [the overwhelming power of the proud]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **pride**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [proud people]

Here, **the hand** represents the power and action of **the wicked**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [and let not the power of the wicked remove me]

David is using the adjective **wicked** as a noun to mean a certain kind of person. Your language may use adjectives in the same way. If not, you could translate this with an equivalent expression. Alternate translation: [those who are wicked]

12.note: If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **iniquity**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [what is wicked]

The expression **are thrust down** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [God has thrust them down]
